blocks.content: Cassandra Hale believed mornings were too important to waste.
Not because she was disciplined. Discipline sounded like something your dentist told you to be.
Intentional. That was the word. Intentional meant iced coffee before breakfast, mismatched socks because they made you smile, the long way through town just because the sky looked dramatic.
She stepped off the bus and took a long sip, cold coffee biting sweetly against her tongue. The air stung her nose. She loved it.
Her phone buzzed.
Did you take it?
Cassandra stared at it for three full seconds, then flipped the phone face-down against her palm.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Not yet.
Maya loved like a locked door. Secure. Protective. Impossible to sneak past. Cassandra loved her for it. She also found it wildly inconvenient.
The arcade sign buzzed ahead, half-awake. Cassandra knocked twice on the glass door and made a dramatic sad face through the window.
Lena appeared between two claw machines — dark curls piled into a messy bun, keys in hand.
She pointed at the door sign.
CLOSED.
Cassandra pointed at herself.
SPECIAL.
Lena rolled her eyes so hard it looked like a medical condition, but she unlocked the door anyway.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: You are a menace.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: A beloved menace. There's a difference.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: The difference is caffeine.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Exactly. Which is why I brought you tea.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: Is this an apology tea or a bribery tea?

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Can't it be both?

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: That depends. What did you do?

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Nothing yet.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: That's somehow worse.
The arcade smelled like dust, sugar, and old carpet. To most people it felt outdated. To Cassandra, it felt alive.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: You're early.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: You say that like it's shocking.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: You're either very early or forty minutes late. There is no middle ground.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I am misunderstood by everyone I know.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: You are understood perfectly. That's the issue.
Lena stirred her tea. Watching.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: Maya texted me.
Cassandra turned toward a machine and pretended to study the jackpot tickets.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Traitor.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: She worries.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: She professionally worries.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: She asked if you took it.
Cassandra's fingers rested against the cold glass of the machine. Her reflection looked back — red hair, bright eyes, a smile still holding where she'd left it.
She looked fine. That was the mercy and cruelty of it.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I will.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: Cass.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I said I will.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: You always say that.
Cassandra turned with a smile sharp enough to cut the conversation in half.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: And I am always charming when I do.
Lena didn't laugh. That was the problem with people who loved you — sometimes they refused to follow the script.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I just want today to feel normal.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: Okay.
No lecture. No argument. Just okay. Cassandra loved her for that too.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Now — if I win that purple dinosaur, you have to admit I'm gifted.

blocks.speaker: Lena
blocks.content: That machine has stolen more money than government taxes.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: Then today we overthrow tyranny.

Cassandra fed a dollar into the machine. For thirty seconds, nothing existed except cheap music, plastic treasure, and the possibility that the impossible could be grabbed if you just lined things up right.
